findings.claim: The hook's Bash-command detection treats any command containing a single or double quote as too complex to parse and silently skips enforcement, so ordinary quoted commands like cat "docs/rules/x.md" bypass the protected-context-file gate entirely.
findings.fix: Do a minimal quote-aware tokenization (or use jq's @sh/word-splitting helpers already available in the script) so a quoted single-argument cat is still recognized, and treat genuinely un-parseable commands as denyable-if-suspicious rather than pass-through.

findings.claim: Three concrete changes in the diff (the read-gate.sh subagent spill requirement, the new 85-line skill-invoke-gate.sh, and the worktree-status page filter rewrite plus Reload button) have no corresponding entry in any plans/v1-2-1 plan, and the first and third contradict explicit plan scope statements ("the hooks stay as-is" and "no template or JS changes at all").
findings.fix: Confirm with the author whether these were intentional, and record each in a Changelog entry in the nearest plan (or a short new plan section) per the repo's plan-as-binding-contract rules.

findings.claim: GitChangedFiles splits git output with strings.Fields (any whitespace) instead of newlines, so a changed path containing a space is split into bogus fragments and ruleDelta/surfaceDelta silently miss the real change, letting a rule file with a space in its name dodge the delta scan in gated/strict mode.
findings.fix: Use strings.Split(diffed, "\n") and the same for untracked, trimming empties, instead of strings.Fields over the concatenation.

findings.claim: internal/shell.RunSync is a near-verbatim copy-paste of internal/shell.Run, identical except the timeout constant and error-message prefix, duplication the repo's own Go guide flags.
findings.fix: Extract a shared runWithTimeout(ctx, dir, timeout, errPrefix, name string, args ...string) used by both, removing ~20 duplicated lines without changing either call site's signature.

findings.claim: TestDistShipsReachCoveredSliceWithBinaries reads the live repo tree via a relative path (repoRoot = "../..") instead of a synthetic fixture, leaving it exposed to interference from external processes in a multi-worktree environment, as seen in one non-reproducible intermittent failure that rewrote the checkout's own acdsl files.
findings.fix: Point the test at a synthetic fixture repo, as TestDistNoCoverageWritesNothing already does, to remove the exposure regardless of the actual cause.

findings.claim: Repo.Label is one of the few new fields with a json omitempty tag while sibling fields Name and Path lack it — consistent with the plan's intent and not a defect, but an asymmetry in an otherwise-uniform struct worth a second pair of eyes.
